messages:
sam: noticed a new pattern of brief soft-429 bursts during the 02:10 UTC traffic spike. looks tied to a KV-prefetch budget exhaustion + kernel swap overhead. attaching quick notes and a config idea.

lee: can you paste the perf numbers? is it kv miss amplification or batcher holdback?

sam: kv miss amplification. graph showed kv miss rate jump ~12% -> ~47% over ~4m, and at the same time continuous-batcher assembly time P95 went from 18ms -> 85ms. overall token latency (model/cpu) p95 up ~60ms.

maria: oh that's nasty. did the kernel hint change for short sequences? we recently flipped prefer-fused-attn on that cluster.

sam: we flipped a kernel preference for short seqs last week. my theory: when KV misses spike, many requests are short but cold, batcher tries to coalesce, kernel selection w/ fused-attn causes longer microbatch assemble because of blocking prefetchs? profiling shows more context-switching.

jon: any traces? small flame or raw stack samples?

sam: grabbed a short perf dump. key lines:

```
# sample summary
KV miss rate: 47% (baseline 12%)
Batch assemble P50/P95: 12ms / 85ms
Model kernel switch cost (avg): 7ms -> 22ms
Queue wait tail (p95): 42ms -> 105ms
Soft-429s spike count: +240 in 4m window
```

zara: hmm. that looks like queue admission should've shed earlier. current token-budget-per-route is flat and we let prefetches burn lanes.

lee: agree. we should try lanes with priority token budgets: fast lane for short seq low-kv-hit routes, prefetch lane with capped background budget. basically separate budgets so prefetches can't exhaust the main admit pool.

maria: +1. also add a quick decay for prefetch allocations after rapid miss-rate increases. i.e. if kv_miss_rate delta > 10% in 60s, halve prefetch token budget for 2m.

sam: prototype admit config (pseudocode):

```
admit_policy: {
  lanes: [
    { name: "interactive", token_budget: 10000, priority: 10 },
    { name: "prefetch", token_budget: 2000, priority: 2, overflow: false }
  ],
  token_targets: {
    interactive: { p95_wait_ms: 50 },
    prefetch: { max_tokens_per_minute: 120000 }
  },
  kv_miss_guard: {
    window_s: 60,
    miss_rate_delta_threshold: 0.10,
    prefetch_budget_multiplier_on_spike: 0.5,
    cooldown_s: 120
  }
}
```

jon: looks reasonable. what about kernel hinting if the batcher sees high assemble time? maybe downgrade fused-attn preference to non-fused variant for the next N batches to avoid stalls.

sam: idea: add a dynamic kernel-preference override keyed by recent assemble latency. if assemble_p95 > 40ms and kv_miss_rate > 25% then prefer non-fused for next 200 batches.

zara: we'll need metrics and a small integration test. can infra-bot run a canary with synthetic kv miss injection?

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary pipeline trigger queued. use flag name: admit-token-lanes-experiment. ETA: ~12m. :white_check_mark:

lee: also add a temporary metric: lane_token_exhaust_count and lane_prefetch_decay_count. this helps correlate prefetch throttles to soft-429 reductions.

maria: for the canary, run two variants: A) lanes + kv_miss_guard, B) lanes + kv_miss_guard + kernel-preference-fallback. compare p95 latencies, soft-429 counts, and model throughput. keep runs short (5m steady-state each) and repeat 3x.

sam: i'll assemble a small reproduction script that drives 200rps with a controllable kv hit ratio. will post results in this thread after canary.

jon: one more thought — ensure that the admit path's quick-path for interactive lane avoids expensive cache checks. micro-ops there should be O(1). if we add extra locking we might reintroduce stalls.

sam: agreed. implementation plan: 1) config + metrics + infra flag 2) implement lane admission in acceptor (no locks, atomic counters) 3) kernel fallback hook in batcher 4) canary runs and compare A/B 5) iterate.

zara: sounds good. please assign PRs and link CI.

sam: assigning initial PRs now. infra-bot created flag admit-token-lanes-experiment and canary job: https://ci.redwood/flags/admit-token-lanes-experiment

infra-bot: canary job started: job/2799991234-admit-lanes-canary, expected finish 18m.

maria: thanks. once we have results we can decide whether to roll to prod with gradual ramp and fallback to current policy. :thumbsup:
